### Report: Add-On Cannabidiol for Dravet Syndrome

**Conclusion:**
The claim is **true**, not false. High-quality clinical trial evidence demonstrates that add-on pharmaceutical cannabidiol (CBD) significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in patients with Dravet syndrome.

**Key Evidence:**
* **Landmark NEJM Trial:** A double-blind, placebo-controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* found that adjunctive cannabidiol reduced monthly convulsive seizure frequency from a median of 12.4 to 5.9, compared to a negligible reduction from 14.9 to 14.1 with placebo over a 14-week period (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618; https://www.ovid.com/journals/nejm/fulltext/10.1056/nejmoa1611618~trial-of-cannabidiol-for-drug-resistant-seizures-in-the).
* **Dose-Ranging Randomized Trial:** A trial reported in *JAMA Neurology* showed that daily adjunctive cannabidiol at doses of 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg reduced convulsive seizure frequency by 48.7% and 45.7% respectively, compared to 26.9% with placebo (https://www.medicinesresources.nhs.uk/dose-ranging-effect-of-adjunctive-oral-cannabidiol-vs-placebo-on-convulsive-seizure-frequency-in-dravet-syndrome-a-randomized-clinical-trial.html).
* **FDA Approval:** Based on these randomized clinical trials, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Epidiolex (purified oral cannabidiol) specifically to treat seizures associated with Dravet syndrome (https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-comprised-active-ingredient-derived-marijuana-treat-rare-severe-forms).
